speaker: Doctor
text: The blood gas results indicate respiratory acidosis with hypoxemia, while your white blood cell count is normal. Is there a history of prolonged labor, meconium staining, or a difficult delivery? Also, has there been any family history of lung disease or sudden infant death syndrome?

speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, born after the 32nd gestational week. The baby was born via cesarean delivery. The mother had gestational diabetes but was otherwise healthy with no other pregnancy-related diseases.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for the history; your prematurity at 32 weeks and maternal gestational diabetes are significant risk factors. Given the respiratory acidosis and hypoxemia, have you noticed any grunting, flaring of the nostrils, or visible chest retractions?

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Chest X-Ray: Ground-glass appearance, air bronchograms, suggesting Respiratory Distress Syndrome (RDS)

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Neonatal Respiratory Distress Syndrome (NRDS) due to prematurity. The clinical picture of 32-week gestation, respiratory acidosis, and the chest X-ray showing ground-glass opacities with air bronchograms is pathognomonic for this condition.
